extracted.intended_audience: users and developers of the PARI/GP computer algebra library (mathematicians, number theorists, and scientific programmers)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP library routines (mostly matrix, vector, lattice and quadratic-form related), describing semantics, flags, return values, error conditions, complexity notes and usage examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: matisdiagonal / isdiagonal
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns true (1) if x is a diagonal matrix, false (0) otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN isdiagonal(GEN x). No examples beyond definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: matker / matker0 / ker / ZM_ker
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives a basis for the kernel of matrix x as columns of a matrix; matrix entries can be any type compatible with generic arithmetic (+, ×, /). If x is known integral, set flag = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN matker0(GEN x, long flag); also GEN ker(GEN x) (flag=0) and GEN ZM_ker(GEN x) (flag=1). Examples show computing kernel modulo arithmetic and typical usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: matkerint / matkerint0 / kerint
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives an LLL-reduced Z-basis for the lattice equal to the kernel of a matrix x with rational entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag parameter is deprecated. Library syntax: GEN matkerint0(GEN x, long flag). Prefer GEN kerint(GEN x) if x is integer; otherwise use Q_primpart first.

rubrics_metrics.name: matkermod
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives a Howell basis (unique representation for submodules of (Z/dZ)^n) for the kernel of matrix x modulo d, as columns of a matrix. x must have t_INT entries; d any positive integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If im is present, it is set to a basis of the image of x (computed on the way). Example demonstrates computing kernel modulo 6. Library syntax: GEN matkermod(GEN x, GEN d, GEN *im = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: matmuldiagonal
rubrics_metrics.description: Product of matrix x by the diagonal matrix whose diagonal entries are those of vector d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent to x * matdiagonal(d) but much faster. Library syntax: GEN matmuldiagonal(GEN x, GEN d).

rubrics_metrics.name: matmultodiagonal
rubrics_metrics.description: Product of matrices x and y assuming the result is a diagonal matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Much faster than general multiplication when result is diagonal; result is undefined if x*y is not diagonal. Library syntax: GEN matmultodiagonal(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: matpascal / matqpascal / matpascal
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates as a matrix the lower triangular Pascal triangle of order n+1 (binomial coefficients up to n). If q is given, computes the q-Pascal triangle using q-binomial coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN matqpascal(long n, GEN q = NULL). Also GEN matpascal(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matpermanent
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the permanent of a square matrix using Ryser's formula in Gray code order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Runs in time O(2^n n) for an n×n matrix and is not implemented for large n. Examples show computing permanent for n=20 on a specific matrix. Library syntax: GEN matpermanent(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matqr
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns [Q,R], the QR-decomposition of a square invertible real matrix M: Q orthogonal, R upper triangular. If flag=1, returns orthogonal factor as a sequence of Householder transforms (more stable and faster to apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=1, return q such that mathouseholder(q, M) approx R and mathouseholder(q, matid(#M)) == Q~ (inverse of Q). Raises error if precision too low or x singular. Library syntax: GEN matqr(GEN M, long flag, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: matrank
rubrics_metrics.description: Rank of matrix x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long rank(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matrix (creator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an m×n matrix whose coefficients are given by the expression expr depending on row X (1..m) and column Y (1..n). If one of parameters X, Y, expr omitted fill with zeroes. If n omitted, return square m×m matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: matrix(m, {n=m}, {X}, {Y}, {expr=0}). Expression has formal parameters for indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: matrixqz
rubrics_metrics.description: Given A ∈ M_{m,n}(Q), behavior depends on p: for p>=0 (default p=0) and A of maximal rank returns integer B with Im_Q B = Im_Q A and the gcd of its n×n minors coprime to p (if p=0 gcd=1). For p=-1 returns HNF basis of Zn ∩ Im_Z A. For p=-2 returns HNF basis of Zn ∩ Im_Q A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate minors and resulting integer matrices. Library syntax: GEN matrixqz0(GEN A, GEN p = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsize
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a vector or matrix x, returns a row vector [#rows, #columns] (1 for a row vector columns, 1 for a column vector rows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN matsize(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsnf
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs the vector of elementary divisors (diagonal of Smith normal form) of X, normalized so that dn | dn-1 | ... | d1. Supports flags for complete output, generic input, cleanup, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary digits of flag: 1 -> complete output [U,V,D]; 2 -> allow polynomial entries (input must be square); 4 -> cleanup (delete elementary divisors equal to 1) and allows X to be already a vector of elementary divisors or [U,V,D]. Library syntax: GEN matsnf0(GEN X, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsolve / gauss / ZM_gauss
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve M X = B for X when M is left-invertible; returns the unique solution if it exists. Uses Dixon p-adic lifting if integral inputs, Gaussian elimination otherwise. If no solution exists returns an X with M X - B non-zero but with many zeros; raises exception if M is not left-invertible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show behavior with overdetermined systems. Works when B is a matrix (returns unique matrix solution if it exists). Library syntax: GEN gauss(GEN M, GEN B); for integral input use GEN ZM_gauss(GEN M, GEN B).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsolvemod / gaussmodulo / gaussmodulo2
rubrics_metrics.description: Given integral matrix M, D a column vector of non-negative integer moduli, and integral B, gives an integer solution X to the system of congruences sum_j m_{i,j} x_j ≡ b_i (mod d_i) if one exists, else returns zero. Shorthand: single integer B or D applied to all components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=1, return all solutions as [x, u] where x is one solution and columns of u span homogeneous solutions. Examples show solving over F_3 and mixed modulus/integer equations. Library syntax: GEN matsolvemod(GEN M, GEN D, GEN B, long flag); GEN gaussmodulo(...)=flag0, gaussmodulo2(...)=flag1.

rubrics_metrics.name: matsupplement / suppl
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming columns of x are linearly independent, finds a square invertible matrix whose first columns are the columns of x (completes to a basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raises error if x has 0 columns (design bug: ambient dimension unknown). Example and error message shown. Library syntax: GEN suppl(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: mattranspose / gtrans
rubrics_metrics.description: Transpose of x (also x~); affects only vectors and matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gtrans(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: minpoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimal polynomial of A with respect to variable v: the monic polynomial P of minimal degree (in v) such that P(A)=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN minpoly(GEN A, long v = -1) where v is a variable number.

rubrics_metrics.name: norml2 / gnorml2
rubrics_metrics.description: Square of the L2-norm of x. If x scalar, defined as squared complex modulus. For polynomials, vectors, matrices defined recursively as sum_i norml2(x_i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show values for vectors and matrices. Real t_QUADs not supported. Library syntax: GEN gnorml2(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: normlp / gnormlp
rubrics_metrics.description: Lp-norm of x; sup norm if p omitted or +oo. For scalar abs(x); for vectors/polynomials/matrices defined recursively: p=+oo -> max of component norms; otherwise ((sum_i normlp(x_i,p)^p)^(1/p)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples with vectors, matrices, polynomials and different p values. Library syntax: GEN gnormlp(GEN x, GEN p = NULL, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfauto
rubrics_metrics.description: For square symmetric integer matrix G (positive definite quadratic form), outputs automorphism group of associated lattice as [o, g] where o is group order and g vector of generators (matrices H satisfying G = tH G H).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computation requires minimal vectors and can be lengthy as dimension grows. Interface experimental. Implementation follows Plesken and Souvignier. Optional qfisominit usage and flag meanings referenced. Library syntax: GEN qfauto0(GEN G, GEN fl = NULL); also GEN qfauto(GEN G, GEN fl) where G may be vector of zm matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: qfautoexport
rubrics_metrics.description: Export automorphism group qfa (as from qfauto) as a string suitable for GAP (flag=0 or absent) or Magma (flag=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows exporting and invoking GAP to compute group order. Library syntax: GEN qfautoexport(GEN qfa, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbil (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete; use qfeval instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN qfbil(GEN x, GEN y, GEN q = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfeval
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate quadratic form q (symmetric matrix) at vector x; if y present evaluate polar form at (x,y). If q omitted, use standard Euclidean scalar product (identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roughly equivalent to x~ * q * y but faster and does not distinguish row/column vectors. Special optimized handling for q=Id and for t_QFI/t_QFR types (avoid denominators). Supports passing x as t_MAT to compute Gram matrix. Many timing examples comparing qfeval to matrix multiplications. Library syntax: GEN qfeval0(GEN q = NULL, GEN x, GEN y = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfgaussred
rubrics_metrics.description: Decomposition into squares of the quadratic form represented by symmetric matrix q: returns matrix whose diagonal entries are coefficients of squares and off-diagonals represent bilinear forms, such that q(x)=sum_i a_ii (x_i + sum_{j>i} a_ij x_j)^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Singular matrices supported (some diagonal coefficients vanish). Example shows 2xy decomposition, and x^2+2xy+y^2. GEN qfgaussred_positive assumes positive definite q and is faster; returns NULL if vector with negative norm occurs. Library syntax: GEN qfgaussred(GEN q).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfisom
rubrics_metrics.description: Given square symmetric integer positive definite matrices G and H, return invertible matrix S such that G = tS H S (isomorphism between lattices). Computation may be long; optional grp (automorphism group of H) can speed up computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: G may be given by qfisominit structure for reuse. Implements Plesken and Souvignier algorithm. Library syntax: GEN qfisom0(GEN G, GEN H, GEN fl = NULL, GEN grp = NULL); GEN qfisom exists where G is vector of zm.

rubrics_metrics.name: qfisominit
rubrics_metrics.description: Given square symmetric integer positive definite G, return an isom structure to speed up computing isomorphisms between G and other forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interface experimental. Optional fl is t_VEC [depth_of_scalar_product_combination, max_level_of_Bacher_polynomials]. Optional m is set of vectors of norm up to maximal diagonal entry of G (matrix or from qfminim). If m omitted, minimal vectors are computed (may be lengthy). Library syntax: GEN qfisominit0(GEN G, GEN fl = NULL, GEN m = NULL) and GEN qfisominit(GEN F, GEN fl) where F may be vector of zm.

rubrics_metrics.name: qfjacobi
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Jacobi's eigenvalue algorithm to real symmetric matrix A. Returns [L, V] where L is vector of real eigenvalues (increasing order) and V is orthogonal matrix of eigenvectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show numerical accuracy: (A-L[i])*H[,i] small and H*H~ close to identity. Library syntax: GEN jacobi(GEN A, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: qflll / qflll0 / lll / lllint / lllkerim
rubrics_metrics.description: LLL algorithm applied to columns of matrix x: returns unimodular transformation T such that x * T is LLL-reduced basis of lattice generated by x columns. Columns may be linearly dependent; T may be non-square if x not maximal rank. Default LLL parameters are (0.51, 0.99).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag meanings: 0 default (rescale/convert to integers if needed), 1 assume integral x (approx GS computations, precision adjusts), 2 partially reduced basis algorithm (Montgomery unpublished) for integer columns linearly independent (faster but not LLL-reduced), 4 return [K, T] where K columns are integer kernel basis and T transforms x to LLL-reduced image, 5 like 4 but x may have polynomial coefficients, 8 same as 0 but x may have polynomial coeffs. Implementation adapted from Nguyen & Stehlé and fplll code. Library syntax: GEN qflll0(GEN x, long flag); aliases: GEN lll(GEN x) (flag=0), GEN lllint(GEN x) (flag=1), GEN lllkerim(GEN x) (flag=4).

rubrics_metrics.name: qflllgram / qflllgram0 / lll-gram
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as qflll but input is Gram matrix G = x~ * x rather than coordinates. G must be square symmetric real matrix corresponding to a quadratic form. Returns unimodular T such that x*T is LLL-reduced basis of lattice generated by x columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag meanings similar to qflll: 0 default (rescale/convert), 1 assume integral G (approx GS precision adjust), 4 kernel and reduced image if G integral, 5 like 4 but polynomial coefficients allowed, 8 etc. Library syntax: GEN qflllgram0(GEN G, long flag); aliases: GEN lll-gram(GEN G) (flag=0), GEN lllgramint(GEN G) (flag=1), GEN lllgramkerim(GEN G) (flag=4).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfminim / qfminim0 / minim / minim2 / minim_raw
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerate vectors of quadratic form x (square symmetric positive definite) with norm ≤ b using Fincke-Pohst algorithm, storing at most m vectors (no limit if m omitted). If b omitted, searches for minimal non-zero vectors. Behavior depends on flag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0 (default): returns at most 2m vectors; result is [number_enumerated, maximum_norm_found, matrix_of_column_vectors] where only one vector per ±v pair returned, at most m pairs unless m omitted; x must have integral entries; uses low-precision floating computations for speed and may error if large rounding errors. flag=1: ignores m and returns [N, v] where v is non-zero vector of length N ≤ b or [] if none; if b omitted returns smallish vector (smallest in LLL-reduced basis). flag=2: robust algorithm allowing non-integral real entries; if b omitted minimal vectors only approximately same norm; m acts as storage upper bound but all minimal vectors enumerated. Examples include Leech lattice minimal vector count and timing. Library syntax: GEN qfminim0(GEN x, GEN b = NULL, GEN m = NULL, long flag, long prec) and aliases GEN minim/G minim2/minim_raw (raw skips LLL reduction and returns NULL on accuracy error).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfnorm (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete; use qfeval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN qfnorm(GEN x, GEN q = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qforbits
rubrics_metrics.description: Return orbits of V under action of group generated by set G of linear transformations. Assumes G contains -identity and input V uses only one of {v,-v}. If G does not stabilize V, returns 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example computes representatives and orbit lengths of vectors of norm ≤ 3 under automorphisms of lattice A6. Library syntax: GEN qforbits(GEN G, GEN V).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfparam
rubrics_metrics.description: Coefficients of binary quadratic forms that parametrize solutions of a ternary quadratic form G using particular solution sol. Optional flag (0/1/2/3) reduces the flag-th form if set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows parameterization producing polynomials in x,y with v~*G*v == 0. Library syntax: GEN qfparam(GEN G, GEN sol, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfperfection
rubrics_metrics.description: Given G (square symmetric integer positive definite), outputs the perfection rank of the form: rank of family of symmetric matrices v_i v_i^t where v_i range over half the minimal vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires computing minimal vectors; can be very lengthy for higher dimensions. Library syntax: GEN perf(GEN G).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfrep
rubrics_metrics.description: Count vectors representing successive integers by quadratic form q. If flag=0 count all vectors; outputs vector whose i-th entry (1≤i≤B) is half number of vectors v with q(v)=i. If flag=1 count vectors of even norm: i-th entry is half number with q(v)=2i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses naive algorithm based on qfminim and will fail if any entry gets larger than 2^31 (or 2^63). Examples given. Library syntax: GEN qfrep0(GEN q, GEN B, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfsign
rubrics_metrics.description: Return [p,m] signature of quadratic form represented by symmetric matrix x: p = number of positive eigenvalues, m = number of negative eigenvalues, computed using Gaussian reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN qfsign(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfsolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve over Q the quadratic equation X^t G X = 0 for square symmetric rational matrix G (n≥1). Returns a non-zero vector or matrix generating a totally isotropic subspace, or an integer indicating obstruction: prime p for no local solution at p, -1 for no real solution, -2 for n=2 and -det G positive but non-square.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show different return codes (prime, -1, -2). Library syntax: GEN qfsolve(GEN G).

rubrics_metrics.name: seralgdep
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a linear relation between powers (1, s, ..., s^p) of series s with polynomial coefficients of degree ≤ r; returns 0 if no relation found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates finding algebraic dependence for a power series. Series main variable must not be x to express result as polynomial in x. Library syntax: GEN seralgdep(GEN s, long p, long r).

rubrics_metrics.name: setbinop
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the set of f(x,y) where x in X and y in Y. If Y omitted assume X=Y and f symmetric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: set sum and difference of sets, set X+X gives 2X. Library syntax: GEN setbinop(GEN f, GEN X, GEN Y = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: setintersect
rubrics_metrics.description: Intersection of two sets x and y. If x or y is not a set, result undefined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See setisset for definition of sets in PARI. Library syntax: GEN setintersect(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: setisset
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns true (1) if x is a set, false (0) otherwise. In PARI a set is a row vector with strictly increasing entries according to universal comparison function. Use Set to convert other objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Set([3,1,1,2]) -> [1,2,3]. Library syntax: long setisset(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: setminus
rubrics_metrics.description: Difference of sets x and y: elements of x not in y. If x or y not a set, result undefined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN setminus(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: setsearch
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether x belongs to set S. If flag=0 or omitted and x ∈ S return index j with S[j]=x, otherwise 0. If flag non-zero return index j where x should be inserted, or 0 if it already belongs to S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default behavior requires S to be a set (sorted, unique). If S is not a set, sorted lists with cmp-compatible order accepted (use listsort first). Examples show wrong results when using unsorted vectors or lists, and usage with listinsert to insert at returned position when flag=1. Library syntax: long setsearch(GEN S, GEN x, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: setunion
rubrics_metrics.description: Union of two sets x and y. If x or y is not a set result undefined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN setunion(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: trace / gtrace
rubrics_metrics.description: General trace operation. For non-matrices equal to sum of x and its conjugate (except polmods where trace as algebraic number). For square matrices ordinary trace. Error if x is non-square matrix (but not a vector).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gtrace(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecextract / extract0
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract components of vector or matrix x according to specifier y. If x matrix and z present, y is row specifier and z column specifier. y may be integer (mask), vector of indices, or string describing ranges and complements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mask interpretation: binary bits of integer read right-to-left correspond to components left-to-right. String forms: single index, 'a..b' range (a or b can be omitted defaults to 1 or -1) and '^' prefix for complement. Range notation v[i..j] and M[i..j,k..l] is faster/simpler but lacks reverse order and omission-of-bounds features. Many examples provided. Library syntax: GEN extract0(GEN x, GEN y, GEN z = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecprod
rubrics_metrics.description: Return product of components of vector v; returns 1 for empty vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: vecprod([1,2,3]) -> 6; vecprod([]) -> 1. Library syntax: GEN vecprod(GEN v).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecsearch
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether x belongs to sorted vector or list v: return positive index if found, 0 if not. If cmpf omitted assume v sorted in increasing order via lex; cmpf can be comparison function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If v unsorted result undefined. cmpf can be integer k to sort by k-th subcomponent, or vector to specify lexicographic component order. For expensive keys, precompute keys and search in key vector. Abuses allowed: x may be matrix considered as vector of columns; t_VEC may be considered when its transpose matches a column. Examples show vecsort + vecsearch. Library syntax: long vecsearch(GEN v, GEN x, GEN cmpf = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecsort
rubrics_metrics.description: Sort vector x in ascending order using mergesort (stable). x must be list, vector or matrix (matrix seen as vector of columns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cmpf omitted use standard lex comparison, restricting element types to integers, fractions, reals and vectors of those; t_VECSMALL allowed. If cmpf present it may be: an integer k (sort by k-th subcomponent), a vector of indices (lexicographic according to those components), or a comparison function. Uses mergesort stability property; initial ordering of equal entries preserved. Library syntax: vecsort(x, {cmpf}, {flag=0}).
